scenarioStory.history: Patient reports sudden onset of palpitations and lightheadedness approximately 10 minutes ago while working. Describes his heart as 'racing' and feels like he might pass out when standing. Denies chest pain, denies any prior episodes like this.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 45-year-old male seated, pale and diaphoretic, reporting sudden-onset palpitations and near-syncope. Radial pulse is rapid and weak. → Unstable pathway recognized: Crew establishes monitoring, IV access, and checks blood glucose while recognizing that the patient's hypotension and near-syncope place him in the unstable regular narrow complex tachycardia pathway, which calls for synchronized cardioversion rather than stable pharmacologic therapy. → Sedation given, cardioversion performed: Crew administers weight-based ketamine for procedural sedation, then delivers a synchronized cardioversion per manufacturer recommendation. → Converted to sinus rhythm: Rhythm converts to sinus following synchronized cardioversion; blood pressure and mental status improve. Crew reassesses vitals, obtains a post-conversion 12-lead, and prepares for transport.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 45-year-old male seated, pale and diaphoretic, reporting sudden-onset palpitations and near-syncope. Radial pulse is rapid and weak.

scenarioEvents.name: Unstable pathway recognized
scenarioEvents.description: Crew establishes monitoring, IV access, and checks blood glucose while recognizing that the patient's hypotension and near-syncope place him in the unstable regular narrow complex tachycardia pathway, which calls for synchronized cardioversion rather than stable pharmacologic therapy.
relatedChecklist: Establish O2, cardiac monitor, 12-lead EKG, and IV access
Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a contributing cause
Recognize hypotension and near-syncope as unstable SVT; bypass the stable pharmacologic pathway

scenarioEvents.name: Sedation given, cardioversion performed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew administers weight-based ketamine for procedural sedation, then delivers a synchronized cardioversion per manufacturer recommendation.
relatedChecklist: Ketamine 22 mg IV for procedural sedation (88 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 22 mg; max initial 25 mg)
Deliver synchronized cardioversion per manufacturer's energy recommendation

scenarioEvents.name: Converted to sinus rhythm
scenarioEvents.description: Rhythm converts to sinus following synchronized cardioversion; blood pressure and mental status improve. Crew reassesses vitals, obtains a post-conversion 12-lead, and prepares for transport.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vitals and rhythm; obtain post-conversion 12-lead EKG

scenarioEvents.name: Vagal/adenosine attempted despite instability
scenarioEvents.description: Crew treats the tachycardia as though stable, attempting vagal maneuvers and adenosine despite the patient's hypotension and near-syncope. Time is lost while the patient's perfusion continues to decline.
relatedChecklist: Abandon the stable pathway; sedate and perform synchronized cardioversion immediately

checklist.title: Establish O2, cardiac monitor, 12-lead EKG, and IV access
Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a contributing cause
Recognize hypotension and near-syncope as unstable SVT; bypass the stable pharmacologic pathway
Ketamine 22 mg IV for procedural sedation (88 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 22 mg; max initial 25 mg)
Deliver synchronized cardioversion per manufacturer's energy recommendation
Reassess vitals and rhythm; obtain post-conversion 12-lead EKG
Abandon the stable pathway; sedate and perform synchronized cardioversion immediately
